chapters.title: Present simple vs present continuous
chapters.summary: Use present simple for routines and general truths, and present continuous for actions in progress or temporary situations.
points: Present simple describes habits and general truths.
Present continuous describes actions happening now.
Present continuous can describe temporary situations.

examples.english: She works in London.
She is working from home this week.

pitfalls: Do not overuse present continuous with stative verbs.

practicePrompts.prompt: Write three sentence pairs contrasting present simple and present continuous.
practicePrompts.instructions: Write three pairs of sentences. In each pair, use the present simple for a routine or general truth and the present continuous for an action in progress or a temporary situation.
practicePrompts.starterText: She works in the office, but this week she is working from home.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: They usually take the train to work, but today they are driving because of the strike. My brother studies economics at university, but this month he is studying for his final exams every evening. We often eat at home on weekdays, but tonight we are eating out with some friends.

chapters.title: Present simple vs present continuous (2)
chapters.summary: Some stative verbs usually prefer the present simple, but the continuous can sometimes be used to emphasize temporariness or change.
points: Many state verbs are more commonly used in the present simple.
The present continuous can highlight temporary behavior or change.

examples.english: I understand the problem.
He is being difficult today.

pitfalls: Not every verb that describes a state sounds natural in the continuous.

practicePrompts.prompt: Rewrite five sentences using the more natural tense.
practicePrompts.instructions: Rewrite five sentences and choose the more natural tense. Use the present simple for stative verbs unless the sentence clearly emphasizes temporary behaviour or change.
practicePrompts.starterText: I understand the problem, but he is being unusually difficult today.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: I understand the problem now. He is being unusually difficult today. We know the manager quite well. She looks tired this week. They prefer remote work, but this month they are trying a hybrid schedule.

chapters.title: Future perfect vs future continuous
chapters.summary: Use the future perfect for actions completed before a future point, and the future continuous for actions in progress at that future time.
points: The future perfect focuses on completion before a future deadline.
The future continuous describes an activity that will be in progress at a specific future moment.
Both forms are useful when giving project updates and planning schedules.

examples.english: By Friday, the team will have finished the draft report.
At 10 a.m. tomorrow, the team will be presenting the proposal.
examples.note: action in progress at a future time

pitfalls: Do not use the future perfect when the meaning is simply a scheduled future action still in progress.

practicePrompts.prompt: Write four sentences about a project timeline using both the future perfect and the future continuous.
practicePrompts.instructions: Write four sentences about a project timeline. Use the future perfect for milestones completed before a future point and the future continuous for work that will still be in progress at that time.
practicePrompts.starterText: By next Wednesday, the design team will have finished the client deck, and at 10 a.m. the product manager will be presenting the revised launch plan.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: By Monday morning, the engineers will have completed the final testing cycle. At the same time, the support team will be preparing the release notes for clients. By the end of the week, we will have updated the onboarding guide for the new feature. During Friday's review meeting, the operations lead will be explaining the rollout timeline to the regional managers.

chapters.title: Mixed conditionals
chapters.summary: Mixed conditionals connect a hypothetical past event with a present result, or a present unreal condition with a past consequence.
points: Use a past unreal clause plus a present result when a different past action would change the current situation.
Use a present unreal clause plus a past result when a different present state would have changed an earlier outcome.
Mixed conditionals are common in reflection, analysis, and professional post-mortems.

examples.english: If we had prepared earlier, we would be in a stronger position now.
If she were more confident, she would have accepted the offer last week.

pitfalls: Do not use a mixed conditional when the sentence simply refers to a past result with no present consequence.

practicePrompts.prompt: Write four sentences using mixed conditionals to reflect on missed opportunities or present consequences.
practicePrompts.instructions: Write four sentences using mixed conditionals to reflect on a past decision and its present result, or a present condition and its past consequence.
practicePrompts.starterText: If we had planned the launch more carefully, we would be in a much stronger position now.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: If the team had tested the feature earlier, we would not be dealing with these client complaints now. If I were more confident in public speaking, I would have accepted the conference invitation last month. If the supplier had delivered on time, the product would be on the market already. If she were better at delegating, she would not have missed the earlier deadline.

chapters.title: Inversion for emphasis
chapters.summary: Formal inversion is used after negative adverbials and limiting expressions to create emphasis and a more advanced written style.
points: Inversion often follows expressions like rarely, never, only then, and not until.
The auxiliary usually comes before the subject when inversion is required.
This pattern is common in formal reports, commentary, and argumentative writing.

examples.english: Rarely have I seen a team respond so quickly to a crisis.
Only after the review did the managers approve the revised plan.

pitfalls: Do not invert after every adverbial; the structure is limited to specific emphatic patterns.

practicePrompts.prompt: Write four formal sentences that use inversion for emphasis after negative or limiting expressions.
practicePrompts.instructions: Write four formal sentences using inversion after negative or limiting expressions such as rarely, never, only then, or not until.
practicePrompts.starterText: Rarely have I seen a proposal generate such immediate support from senior management.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: Rarely have I seen a project team recover so quickly after a major delay. Only after the audit did the board understand the full scale of the problem. Not until the final review did the client approve the revised schedule. Never had the department faced such a complex negotiation before the merger talks began.

chapters.title: Applying for a job
chapters.summary: Vocabulary for job ads, cover letters, applications and career-related language.
points: A cover letter should highlight relevant experience and suitability for the role.
Job ads often mention career prospects, training and salary expectations.
Applications should stand out clearly and professionally.

examples.english: Please find attached my CV in support of my application.
The post offers excellent career prospects.

pitfalls: Do not confuse a cover letter with a CV.
Avoid overly casual language in job applications.

practicePrompts.prompt: Write a short cover letter for an entry-level role.
practicePrompts.instructions: Write a short formal cover letter that introduces your application, highlights relevant experience, and explains why you are suitable for the role.
practicePrompts.starterText: Dear Hiring Manager, I am writing to apply for the entry-level marketing assistant role advertised on your website.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: Dear Hiring Manager, I am writing to apply for the entry-level marketing assistant role advertised on your website. During my studies and internship, I developed strong communication skills and gained experience preparing social media content and supporting event planning. I am especially interested in this post because it offers excellent training and career prospects, and I believe my enthusiasm and attention to detail would make me a strong fit for your team. Please find attached my CV in support of my application. I look forward to hearing from you.

practicePrompts.prompt: List five phrases commonly used in job advertisements.
practicePrompts.instructions: List five phrases that commonly appear in job advertisements. Use authentic recruitment language rather than general business words.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: competitive salary; excellent career prospects; full training provided; relevant prior experience required; strong communication skills

chapters.title: Job interviews
chapters.summary: Vocabulary and phrases used in job interviews, including preparation, confidence, first impressions, interview panels and job offers.
points: Candidates may be shortlisted for interview based on selection criteria.
It is important to do your homework before an interview.
Body language and first impressions matter.
Candidates may be asked about previous roles, responsibilities and notice period.
A job offer may include salary, benefits and reporting structure.

examples.english: I was shortlisted for an interview last week.
We believe your qualifications are an ideal fit for the role.
My notice period is two weeks.

pitfalls: Do not confuse a line manager with an interview panel.
Do not use overly casual language when discussing experience in an interview.

practicePrompts.prompt: Write five interview questions and model answers.
practicePrompts.instructions: Write five realistic interview questions and a short model answer for each one. Keep the tone formal and job-focused.
practicePrompts.starterText: I was shortlisted for an interview last week.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: Question: Why do you want this role? Answer: I am interested in this role because it matches my experience in customer service and offers strong career development. Question: What are your main strengths? Answer: My main strengths are communication, organisation, and the ability to work well under pressure. Question: Describe a challenge you faced. Answer: In my previous role, I had to resolve a delivery problem quickly, so I coordinated with the supplier and kept the client informed throughout. Question: How do you prepare for deadlines? Answer: I prioritise tasks, break projects into smaller steps, and communicate early if any issue may affect the deadline. Question: When could you start? Answer: My notice period is two weeks, so I could start shortly after that.

practicePrompts.prompt: Describe a previous role using formal interview language.
practicePrompts.instructions: Describe a previous role in a formal interview style. Mention responsibilities, achievements, and what you learned from the experience.
practicePrompts.starterText: In my previous role as a sales assistant, I was responsible for handling customer enquiries and supporting the store manager.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: In my previous role as a sales assistant, I was responsible for handling customer enquiries, organising stock, and supporting the store manager during busy periods. I also helped train new team members and contributed to a noticeable improvement in customer satisfaction scores. This experience strengthened my communication skills, taught me how to prioritise tasks under pressure, and showed me the importance of maintaining a professional attitude at all times.

practicePrompts.prompt: Draft a short acceptance email for a job offer.
practicePrompts.instructions: Draft a short professional email accepting a job offer. Mention the role, gratitude, and your expected start arrangements.
practicePrompts.starterText: Dear Ms Patel, thank you for offering me the position of Operations Assistant.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: Dear Ms Patel, thank you for offering me the position of Operations Assistant. I am pleased to accept the role and appreciate the confidence you have shown in my application. I understand that my start date will be 3 May, following my two-week notice period, and I look forward to joining the team. Please let me know if you need any further documents before then. Kind regards, Ana Torres

chapters.title: Job ad analysis
chapters.summary: Reading practice focused on identifying the main offer, required profile and overall tone in a job advertisement.
points: Strong job ads explain the role, training and career prospects clearly.
Candidates should identify the required profile and the benefits that are being emphasized.
The tone is usually persuasive but professional.

examples.english: The post offers excellent career prospects and structured training.

pitfalls: Do not confuse the core responsibilities with the optional benefits.

practicePrompts.prompt: CityBridge Consulting is looking for a junior operations assistant to support client projects, coordinate schedules, and prepare internal reports. The role includes structured training, regular mentoring, and clear career progression for candidates who show initiative. Applicants should have strong communication skills, good attention to detail, and the ability to work calmly under pressure. Previous internship experience is helpful, but we are mainly looking for people who learn quickly and write professionally.
practicePrompts.instructions: Read the advertisement and summarize the role, the ideal candidate, and the overall tone in three or four sentences.
practicePrompts.starterText: The advertisement is for a junior operations assistant role at CityBridge Consulting.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: The advertisement is for a junior operations assistant role that combines project support, scheduling, and report preparation. It is aimed at candidates with strong communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to stay calm under pressure, while making it clear that fast learning matters more than extensive experience. The tone is professional and encouraging because it highlights structured training, mentoring, and clear career progression.

chapters.title: Interview panel summary
chapters.summary: Listening practice focused on the final decision and contrasting details in an interview discussion.
points: The panel values strong preparation and clear examples from previous roles.
One interviewer is impressed by the candidate's communication skills, but another worries about limited leadership experience.
The final position is positive overall, although the panel wants one more example of handling deadlines.

examples.english: She gave clear examples from her previous role, but the panel still asked for more detail about deadlines.

pitfalls: Do not miss the final recommendation just because one concern is mentioned along the way.

practicePrompts.prompt: The panel agrees that the candidate communicated confidently and gave strong examples from her customer service role, but one interviewer notes that she did not fully explain how she manages multiple deadlines. In the end, the panel decides to move her to the next stage because her preparation and communication are stronger than those of the other candidates.
practicePrompts.instructions: Listen to the panel summary and write a short summary of the final decision plus the main reservation that was raised.
practicePrompts.starterText: The panel decides to move the candidate forward, but they still want more detail about her experience with deadlines.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: The panel decides to move the candidate to the next stage because her preparation and communication are stronger than those of the other applicants. However, one interviewer still wants a clearer example of how she manages multiple deadlines. The final judgment is positive overall, but that reservation remains important.

chapters.title: Interview self-introduction
chapters.summary: Speaking practice focused on introducing previous experience and strengths in an interview.
points: A strong interview introduction should identify the previous role, key responsibilities, and one relevant strength.
Candidates should connect experience to the role they are applying for.
A clear connector helps the answer sound more fluent and structured.

examples.english: In my previous role, I supported customer projects and learned how to communicate clearly under pressure.

pitfalls: Do not give a list of unrelated facts without explaining why they matter for the role.

practicePrompts.prompt: You are in a job interview. Introduce your previous role, describe two responsibilities, and explain one strength that makes you a good fit for the position.
practicePrompts.instructions: Answer aloud as if you were introducing yourself in a job interview. Mention your previous role, two responsibilities, and one strength that connects directly to the new role.
practicePrompts.starterText: In my previous role as a customer support assistant, I handled client requests, updated internal records, and learned how to communicate clearly under pressure. However, my biggest strength is staying organised while still keeping a professional tone with clients.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: In my previous role as a customer support assistant, I managed client enquiries and coordinated follow-up tasks with the operations team. I was also responsible for updating internal records and making sure urgent issues were escalated quickly. However, the main strength I would bring to this position is clear communication, because I learned how to explain problems calmly and keep both clients and colleagues informed. That experience makes me a strong fit for a role that depends on organisation and professional communication.

chapters.title: Meeting minutes analysis
chapters.summary: Reading practice focused on tracing decisions, reservations and action points in formal meeting minutes.
points: Meeting minutes usually separate the final decision from background discussion.
A reservation or condition can change the practical meaning of an approved plan.
Action points reveal who owns the next steps after the meeting.

examples.english: The committee approved the phased rollout, subject to additional support training.

pitfalls: Do not confuse a proposed idea with the final approved decision.

practicePrompts.prompt: The minutes note that the team approved a phased product launch for July, provided the support team receives extra training by mid-June. Marketing asked for a wider campaign, but the chair decided to keep the first release limited to three markets so that technical issues could be handled more carefully. The final action items assign training materials to the support lead and customer-facing FAQs to marketing.
practicePrompts.instructions: Read the meeting minutes and summarize the final decision, the condition attached to it, and one action item in three or four sentences.
practicePrompts.starterText: The minutes show that the team approved a phased launch, but only on the condition that extra support training is completed first.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: The minutes show that the team approved a phased product launch for July rather than a wider immediate rollout. However, the approval is conditional because the support team must complete extra training by mid-June. The chair also kept the first release limited to three markets so that technical issues could be managed more carefully. One concrete action item is that the support lead must prepare the training materials while marketing produces the client-facing FAQs.

chapters.title: Deadline renegotiation call
chapters.summary: Listening practice focused on the final agreement and the main concern raised in a deadline negotiation.
points: A negotiation may end positively even when one side raises a serious concern.
The speaker's final agreement is often qualified by one condition or monitoring step.
Deadline language often combines reassurance with a request for interim updates.

examples.english: We can accept the revised date, but we will need a progress update by Tuesday.

pitfalls: Do not focus only on the delay itself and miss the condition attached to the new deadline.

practicePrompts.prompt: The client says they understand the technical issue that delayed the release and are willing to accept a revised delivery date of 18 June. However, they stress that the project cannot slip again because the board review is scheduled for the following week. The call ends with an agreement that the team will send a written progress update by Tuesday and confirm final testing by Friday.
practicePrompts.instructions: Listen to the call summary and write a short summary of the final agreement plus the main condition attached to the revised deadline.
practicePrompts.starterText: The client accepts the revised delivery date, but they insist on a written progress update before the board review.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: The client agrees to move the delivery date to 18 June because they understand the technical issue that caused the delay. However, they make it clear that the deadline cannot slip again because the board review is scheduled for the following week. The agreement therefore includes a written progress update by Tuesday and confirmation of final testing by Friday.

chapters.title: Project update briefing
chapters.summary: Speaking practice focused on concise project updates that balance completed work, current progress and one active risk.
points: A strong project briefing explains what has been completed before moving to current tasks.
Managers expect at least one risk or dependency to be flagged clearly.
Connectors help the update sound structured rather than improvised.

examples.english: We have completed the first testing cycle, and we are now preparing the client-facing documentation.

pitfalls: Do not give a list of disconnected tasks without explaining the current risk or next step.

practicePrompts.prompt: Give a short project update to a manager. Mention what has been completed, what is still in progress, and one risk that needs attention.
practicePrompts.instructions: Give a short spoken update to a manager. Mention one completed task, one task still in progress, and one risk that needs attention.
practicePrompts.starterText: We have finished the first testing cycle, and we are now preparing the client documentation. However, the biggest current risk is that supplier approval may arrive later than expected.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: We have completed the first testing cycle and shared the internal results with the product lead. At the moment, the team is preparing the client documentation and updating the onboarding guide for launch. However, the main risk is that supplier approval may arrive later than expected, which could delay the final sign-off. If that happens, we will need to adjust the release sequence and keep the client informed immediately.

chapters.title: Delay update email
chapters.summary: Writing practice focused on explaining a delay, maintaining a professional tone and proposing a revised plan.
points: A good delay update names the problem clearly without sounding defensive.
Professional emails should explain the revised plan and next checkpoint.
The tone should remain calm, responsible and solution-focused.

examples.english: Unfortunately, the client pack will be ready one day later than planned, but we will send the revised version by Thursday afternoon.

pitfalls: Do not apologize repeatedly without explaining the revised plan and next step.

practicePrompts.prompt: Write a short professional email explaining a delivery delay, the reason for it, and the revised plan.
practicePrompts.instructions: Write a short professional email that explains the delay, gives the reason, apologizes once, and states the revised plan clearly.
practicePrompts.starterText: Dear Ms Rivera, I am writing to let you know that the delivery pack will arrive later than planned because our final approval has taken longer than expected.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: Dear Ms Rivera, I am writing to let you know that the delivery pack will arrive one day later than planned because the final approval stage has taken longer than expected. I apologise for the inconvenience this may cause. We will send the revised version by Thursday afternoon and confirm receipt as soon as it is delivered. To prevent any further delay, I will also send you a progress update tomorrow morning. Kind regards, Daniel Soto

chapters.title: Client escalation call
chapters.summary: Listening practice focused on identifying the final concession in a client escalation and the immediate recovery step that follows.
points: Escalation calls often begin with frustration but end with a negotiated action plan.
The client's main concern may remain, even after a partial concession is offered.
Strong summaries capture both the final agreement and the first immediate next step.

examples.english: We can extend the deadline by forty-eight hours, but we need a revised implementation plan before the end of today.

pitfalls: Do not focus only on the complaint and miss the concrete action that closes the call.

practicePrompts.prompt: The client says the delayed rollout has already affected two regional teams and insists that the situation cannot continue into next week. After reviewing the options, the account manager agrees to extend the deadline by forty-eight hours, but only if the project lead sends a revised implementation plan by 5 p.m. and joins a follow-up call tomorrow morning. The conversation ends with the client saying they still expect weekly status updates until the rollout is stable.
practicePrompts.instructions: Listen to the escalation summary and explain the final concession, the immediate requirement attached to it, and the longer follow-up expectation.
practicePrompts.starterText: The account manager grants a forty-eight-hour extension, but only if the project lead sends a revised plan by 5 p.m.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: The call ends with the account manager granting a forty-eight-hour extension because the client says the current delay has already affected two regional teams. However, the concession is conditional, since the project lead must send a revised implementation plan by 5 p.m. and join a follow-up call the next morning. The client also makes it clear that weekly status updates will still be expected until the rollout is stable.

chapters.title: Handover briefing
chapters.summary: Speaking practice focused on handing over a project clearly by naming current status, priorities and one unresolved risk.
points: A handover should state what has already been completed before moving to outstanding tasks.
Priorities need to be ordered clearly so the next person knows what matters first.
A useful handover also flags one unresolved issue that may require quick attention.

examples.english: I have finished the client notes and uploaded the revised schedule, but the legal approval is still pending.

pitfalls: Do not give isolated task details without making the current priority and the unresolved risk explicit.

practicePrompts.prompt: You are handing over a live project to a colleague before going on leave. Explain what has already been completed, what the top priority is for tomorrow, and one unresolved risk they should monitor.
practicePrompts.instructions: Give a spoken handover that explains what is finished, what tomorrow's priority is, and one unresolved risk the next person should monitor closely.
practicePrompts.starterText: I have finished the client notes and uploaded the revised schedule. Tomorrow's first priority is confirming the supplier timeline, but the unresolved risk is that legal approval may still arrive late.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: I have completed the client notes, uploaded the revised schedule, and shared the latest budget comments with the operations lead. The top priority for tomorrow is confirming the supplier timeline before the regional team begins implementation. However, the main unresolved risk is that legal approval may still arrive late, which could delay the final sign-off. If that happens, the next step should be to warn the client immediately and adjust the handover plan.

chapters.title: Vendor status update call
chapters.summary: Listening practice focused on supplier updates where a reassuring headline is qualified by one operational risk or dependency.
points: Status calls often sound positive at first, but a later qualification can change the practical meaning.
Operational risks are frequently linked to approvals, shipping windows or technical sign-off.
A strong summary should capture both the reassuring headline and the risk that remains.

examples.english: Most components will arrive on schedule, although customs clearance may still delay the final batch.

pitfalls: Do not summarise the update as fully positive if the speaker later adds a dependency that could affect delivery.

practicePrompts.prompt: The supplier says that most of the components have now left the warehouse and should arrive on schedule by Thursday. However, they explain that the final batch is still waiting for customs clearance, so there is a small risk that the installation team may need to begin without the spare units. The call ends with an agreement that the supplier will confirm the customs update by noon tomorrow and arrange direct delivery to the site if needed.
practicePrompts.instructions: Listen to the supplier update and summarize the reassuring headline, the remaining delivery risk, and the agreed next step.
practicePrompts.starterText: Most components are on schedule, but the spare units may still be delayed by customs clearance.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: The supplier says that most of the components have already left the warehouse and should still arrive on schedule by Thursday. However, the final batch of spare units is still waiting for customs clearance, so installation may begin without them if the clearance is delayed. The agreed next step is that the supplier will confirm the customs update by noon tomorrow and arrange direct delivery to the site if necessary.

chapters.title: Stakeholder recommendation pitch
chapters.summary: Speaking practice focused on giving a concise recommendation, supporting it with evidence and acknowledging one trade-off.
points: A strong recommendation states the preferred option early instead of delaying the conclusion.
Decision-makers expect at least one concrete reason or piece of evidence supporting the recommendation.
More advanced responses acknowledge one trade-off without weakening the main recommendation.

examples.english: I recommend the phased rollout because it reduces operational risk, although it will delay the full launch by two weeks.

pitfalls: Do not present several options equally if the task requires a clear recommendation and justification.

practicePrompts.prompt: You are briefing senior stakeholders. Recommend one of two rollout options, give the strongest reason for your choice, and acknowledge one trade-off or limitation.
practicePrompts.instructions: Give a short spoken recommendation to senior stakeholders. State your preferred option early, justify it with one strong reason, and acknowledge one trade-off.
practicePrompts.starterText: I recommend the phased rollout because it reduces operational risk, although it will delay the full launch by two weeks.
practicePrompts.modelAnswer: I recommend the phased rollout because it reduces operational risk and gives the support team time to handle early issues before the wider release. The strongest reason for this option is that it protects the client experience while the team confirms that the new process is stable. However, the trade-off is that the full launch will take longer, so some commercial targets may move back by two weeks. Even so, the lower risk makes this the stronger option overall.
